en.name: Thai eggplant
en.summary: Thai eggplants are the small, firm, golf-ball-sized green fruits quartered into curries, crunchier and more bitter than a large purple aubergine. No figure is published for them, so treat them like eggplant: about 5–7 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
en.pantry: Thai eggplants should not be kept at room temperature for long. They are small and firm, so they look robust, but they lose water steadily and go spongy, and any bruise turns brown then soft. There is no room-temperature figure here and none should be assumed. Refrigerate them whole, with the green calyx still on, as soon as you get home.
en.fridge: Keep the green calyx on — it is the cap that protects the stem end, which is where these fruits go first — and store them whole in the crisper at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where about 5–7 days is the working limit. That figure is borrowed from eggplant, since nothing is published for Thai eggplant. Do not cut them until you cook: the cut halves brown almost immediately, so drop them into salted water the moment you quarter them and leave them there until they go in the pan.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for Thai eggplant and freezing it raw is not worth doing. The whole point of these fruits in a curry is the slight crunch against a soft sauce, and freezing collapses that entirely — what thaws is brown and spongy. If you have too many, use them up in a curry and freeze the finished curry, which keeps far more of what you wanted than a bag of raw quarters would.
spoilage: Fruit gone soft or spongy when squeezed, rather than firm
Browning or shrivelling around the stem end and under the calyx
Wrinkled skin, or soft brown patches where it was bruised
Flesh gone brown and pulpy when cut across
tips: Choose firm, glossy fruit with a fresh green calyx and no browning underneath.
Leave the calyx on until you cook.
Quarter them straight into salted water to stop them browning.
Do not overcook them — the slight crunch is the reason they are in the curry.

faq.q: How long do Thai eggplants last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 5–7 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, kept whole with the calyx on. That figure is borrowed from eggplant; none is published for Thai eggplant.
No timeline exists and it is not worth doing raw — they thaw brown and spongy. Cook them into a curry and freeze that instead.

faq.q: Why do cut Thai eggplants go brown so fast?
faq.a: The flesh oxidises on contact with air, like an apple. Cut them straight into salted water and leave them there until the moment they go in the pan.
Mildly, yes, and that bitterness is part of what they contribute to a green curry. Very seedy, yellowing fruit is more bitter; choose firm green ones.

zh.name: 泰國茄子
zh.summary: 泰國茄子是高爾夫球大小、結實的綠色小茄子，切四瓣下咖哩用，比大顆的紫茄更脆、也更帶苦味。它沒有公布的保存數據，可以比照茄子來看：4°C 以下冷藏約 5～7 天。
zh.pantry: 泰國茄子不適合在室溫放久。它小而結實，看起來很耐操，但實際上會持續失水變成海綿狀，而任何碰傷處都會先變褐再變軟。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。買回家請整顆連著綠色蒂萼一起冷藏。
zh.fridge: 請保留綠色的蒂萼——那頂「帽子」保護著蒂頭，而蒂頭正是這種果實最先壞掉的地方——整顆放在 4°C 以下的蔬果保鮮室，約 5～7 天是工作上限。這個數字是比照茄子而來，因為泰國茄子本身沒有公布的數據。要煮之前才切：切面幾乎立刻褐變，所以切開的當下就丟進鹽水裡，一直泡到下鍋為止。
zh.freezer: 泰國茄子沒有冷凍保存期限，生凍也不值得。它在咖哩裡的全部意義，就是在軟綿的醬汁中那一點脆度，而冷凍會把它整個毀掉——解凍後是褐色的海綿。真的太多的話，就煮成一鍋咖哩再把成品冷凍，保留下來的東西比一袋生切四瓣多太多了。
spoilage: 捏起來變軟或呈海綿狀，而不是結實
蒂頭周圍和蒂萼底下發褐、皺縮
表皮起皺，或碰傷處出現褐色軟斑
tips: 挑結實光亮、蒂萼翠綠、底下沒有褐變的。
要煮之前才把蒂萼摘掉。
切好直接丟進鹽水，防止褐變。
不要煮過頭——那一點脆度正是它出現在咖哩裡的理由。

faq.q: 泰國茄子放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏、整顆連著蒂萼，約 5～7 天。這個數字是比照茄子而來；泰國茄子本身沒有公布的數據。
沒有對應的期限，生凍也不值得——解凍後會變褐變海綿。請煮成咖哩再把成品冷凍。

faq.q: 泰國茄子切開為什麼很快變黑？
faq.a: 果肉一接觸空氣就氧化，跟蘋果一樣。切好立刻丟進鹽水，泡到下鍋那一刻再撈起來。
會帶一點苦，而那份苦正是它在綠咖哩裡的貢獻之一。籽太多、開始泛黃的果實更苦，請挑結實翠綠的。
